events.title: #ThisIsHWS, Outdoor Fun & Sno Cones, and Meet Us By The Lake!
events.summary: #ThisIsHWS #ThisIsHWS is built on a simple idea: every member of the HWS community has a story worth telling. Since 2018, the project has invited students to share the experiences, values, and beliefs that have shaped their lives, creating opportunities to see one another beyond first impressions. Through active listening and storytelling, our community develops authentic empathy and celebrates the individual members that create this community. Outdoor Fun & Sno Cones Get moving and meet new friends at this action-packed recreation session hosted by the HWS Rec Center! Jump into a game of volleyball, badminton, spikeball, kickball, or gaga ball, toss a football, and try a variety of other lawn games and activities. Whether you're looking for some friendly competition or just want to have fun, there's something for everyone. Come play, connect, and discover all the ways you can stay active at HWS! Meet Us By The Lake! There's no better way to experience HWS than on the shores of Seneca Lake! Join us at the Bozzuto Boathouse to paddleboard, kayak, swim, cast a line with members of the Fishing Club, or simply relax and take in the view. Whether you're looking for adventure or a chance to connect with new friends, this is your opportunity to discover one of the most iconic parts of the HWS experience. Come see why life is better when you meet us by the lake! This lake excursion will be offered during your group’s assigned time. You will be escorted from the Quad in small groups with a guide to the boathouse. OM Groups 1-12 1-2:30 p.m. #ThisIsHWS - Vandervort Room 2:45-4 p.m. Outdoor Fun & Sno Cones - The Quad 4:15-5:30 p.m. Meet Us By The Lake! - Bozzuto Boathouse OM Groups 13-25 1-2:30 p.m. Meet Us By The Lake! - Bozzuto Boathouse 2:45-4 p.m. #ThisIsHWS - Vandervort Room 4:15-5:30 p.m. Outdoor Fun & Sno Cones - The Quad OM Groups 26-36 1-2:30 p.m. Outdoor Fun & Sno Cones - The Quad 2:45-4 p.m. Meet Us By The Lake! - Bozzuto Boathouse 4:15-5:30 p.m. #ThisIsHWS - Vandervort Room

The Stern Family Forum is open to the public. Registration information and additional event details will be announced closer to the event.

events.title: Trias Reading: Ann Lauterbach
events.summary: Join us for a reading with poet and essayist Ann Lauterbach. Her eleventh poetry collection, Door, was published in March 2023; previous volumes include Spell (2018), Under the Sign (2013), and Or to Begin Again (2009), which was nominated for a National Book Award. Lauterbach's prose was collected in The Night Sky: Writings on the Poetics of Experience (2008) and The Given & The Chosen (2011). Recent essays include “Mina Loy: Art of the Unbeautiful True” in Mina Loy: Strangeness is Inevitable (2023) and Topos Non Topos: Notes on David Novros for the Paula Cooper Gallery (2023). Her poems have been translated into German, French and Spanish. Among her awards are a Guggenheim Fellowship and a John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Fellowship. She was co-chair of writing in Bard’s MFA Program from 1992 to 2020 and is the Ruth and David Schwab Professor of Languages and Literature.

events.title: Leader in Residence: Morgan Hopkins '10
events.summary: Morgan Hopkins is a seasoned policy strategist and advocate with over a decade of experience. She is best known for her decade-long tenure at All* Above All and its political arm, the All* Above All Action Fund, where she rose from Political Director to Interim Executive Director and ultimately to President. Hopkins was with All* Above All from its inception, advancing historic efforts like the introduction of the EACH Act and the Abortion Justice Act in Congress. She also designed the strategies that resulted in then-candidate Biden's flip-flop on the Hyde amendment and his release of a Presidential budget without Hyde. She was a consistent and vocal presence in national media, appearing in outlets including NPR, The New York Times, The Hill, New York Magazine, Yahoo, The Cut and Politico as a commentator on politics and abortion rights. Now, Hopkins runs both a consulting business and a travel business, selling $500,000 in travel in her first year. Her consulting work includes large-scale event management for nonprofit organizations and serving as Chief of Staff to a healthcare tech angel investor.

events.title: First Generation Celebration
events.summary: Join us as we celebrate and recognize the experiences, accomplishments and contributions of first-generation students, faculty and staff. This gathering is an opportunity to connect, share in community and celebrate the unique journeys of those who are the first in their families to attend college. Nov. 8 marks the anniversary of the signing of the Higher Education Act of 1965 by President Lyndon B. Johnson. The act expanded higher education access, created federal financial aid and launched programs like Federal TRIO to support limited-income and first-generation students. The inaugural national celebration of First-Generation Day took place on Nov. 8, 2017, organized by the Council for Opportunity in Education (COE) and FirstGen Forward. We recognize this date and welcome all first-generation students, faculty, and staff to join us in community on Friday, Nov. 6.

events.title: Opening Reception: Activating the Static: Depicting Motion in Art
events.summary: Join us for the opening reception of Activating the Static: Depicting Motion in Art. Refreshments will be served. This exhibition runs November 19 – December 18, 2026 There is an undeniable challenge presented to an artist when they desire to illustrate motion with a static medium. To express movement in a painting, print, drawing or sculpture often requires manipulating elements such as line, color and texture, and utilizing repetition and different brushstrokes. Through these techniques artists can make ocean waves crash, a woman’s dress twirl around her body, horses gallop, smoke billow and birds fly through the sky. Activating the Static: Depicting Motion in Art examines artworks that appear to be moving, while technically still, through techniques used by artists to create illusions that insinuate active motion. Image: Zeng Shanqing (b. Beijing, 1932-2020), Four Horsemen, 1978, ink on paper. Collection of Hobart and William Smith. Hours: Monday-Friday: 9:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Saturday: 1-3 p.m. Or by appointment, call (315) 781-3487
